REAL-TIME DOUBLE-DIFFERENCE EARTHQUAKE CATALOG FOR NORTHERN CALIFORNIA

Software version: DDRT-3.0.ncsn.

Felix Waldhauser and David Schaff
Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, Columbia University

Contact: felixw@ldeo.columbia.edu 

This dynamic catalog is automatically updated and maintained as new events occur 
and previous events are revised. As a result, hypocenter locations and origin 
times may change over time. When referring to this catalog please use 
Waldhauser (2009) and indicate the catalog version number. 
 
BRIEF DESCRIPTION:
This file includes real-time double-difference (DDRT) hypocenter locations of 
earthquakes recorded by the Northern California Seismic System (NCSS). The DDRT
process relocates new earthquakes relative to a high-resolution double-difference 
catalog of background seismicity. Differential times between a new event and its 
neighboring (reference) events in the DD base catalog are computed from NCSS phase 
arrival time data and by waveform cross-correlation. Waveforms of new events are 
accessed from the real-time DART server at the Northern California Earthquake Data 
Center (NCEDC) in Berkeley. Data associated with the reference events are accessed 
from a locally stored copy of the entire Northern CA seismic archive. For more 
details on the DDRT process see Waldhauser (2009), and on the generation of the DD 
base catalog see Waldhauser and Schaff (2008) and Schaff and Waldhauser (2005).

NOTE: Earthquakes for which no real-time DD solution could be obtained are also 
included in this catalog. They are reported at their orginal, standard 
Hypoinverse event location and labeled HINV. 

REFERENCES:
Waldhauser, F., Near-real-time double-difference event location using long-term 
    seismic archives, with application to Northern California, Bull. Seism. Soc. 
    Am., 99, 2736-2848, doi:10.1785/0120080294, 2009.
Waldhauser, F. and D.P. Schaff (2008), Large-scale relocation of two decades of
    Northern California seismicity using cross-correlation and double-difference 
    methods, J. Geophys. Res., 113, B08311, doi:10.1029/2007JB005479.
Schaff, D.P. and F. Waldhauser (2005), Waveform Cross-Correlation-Based 
    Differential Travel-Time Measurements at the Northern California Seismic 
    Network, Bull. Seism. Soc. Am., 95, 2446-2461.

DATA SOURCES:
The following institutions contribute data to the NCSS system:
U.S. Geological Survey, Menlo Park; University of California, Berkeley; California 
Institute of Technology; University of Nevada, Reno; California Division of Water 
Resources; University of Utah; University of Southern California. Seismic archives 
were obtained from the Northern California Earthquake Data Center (NCEDC) and the 
Northern California Seismic Network (NCSN).

FORMAT DESCRIPTION:
DATE......... Year, Month, Day
TIME......... Hour, Minute, Second
LAT/LON...... Location
DEP.......... Depth [km]
EX/EY/EZ...   Formal least-squares relative location errors (in km) in 
    	      east-west, north-south, and vertical direction at the 95% 
              confidence level.
MAG.......... Magnitude, ML, as listed in the NCSN catalog. 
ID........... CUSP event ID.
VER.......... Solution version, "AA.BB". 
              AA= version of routine NCSS solution used as input for DDRT. 
              BB= DDRT version.
BASE......... Double-difference base catalog used to compute DDRT solution. 
METH......... Method used to compute location. 
              DDRT-X= real-time double-difference, + software version
              HINV= standard Hypoinverse (i.e., original NCSN solution; no 
              DDRT solution possible).
